newsitem.title: USA: Mellon Bank wins breast-feeding award.
newsitem.headline: Mellon Bank wins breast-feeding award.

text.p: Mellon Bank Corp won an award Tuesday from the Allegheny County Health Department for offering special facilities for working mothers who breast-feed their babies.
The bank was honoured with the 1997 Breast-feeding Friendly Workplace Award, said Peggy O'Malley, manager of the health department's breast-feeding promotion programme.
The health department began the award programme last year to recognise area companies that help nursing mothers. A Pittsburgh law firm was last year's winner.
A Mellon spokesman said the bank's headquarters in downtown Pittsburgh contains a "special needs" room in which employees are permitted to breast-feed.
"We thought it was unique that a large corporation would set aside a room for this," said Dave Zazac, a health department spokesman. He said such facilities are rare at large companies.

In addition to an award certificate, Mellon will receive a free six-month rental of an electric breast pump, a cooler case, a nursing stool and breast-feeding books, all courtesy of Medela Inc, a manufacturer of breast pumps.

O'Malley said employer support is often a decisive factor in whether a nursing mom continues to breast-feed once she returns to work. She said more than 50 percent of mothers breastfeed their newborns in the beginning, but the rate drops to just 20 percent six months later, due in part to a lack of breast-feeding support on the job.
